messages.content: Now do the hotel comparison for Boston. We need four nights, Friday January 22 through Tuesday January 26, for Daniel, Owen, and me. The Saturday celebration is at 10 Garden Street in Cambridge. Verify that the room actually takes three people; don't rely on a search result that only shows one bed.

I’ll verify the hotel’s stated maximum occupancy and the actual sleeping setup, then compare the four-night total including tax and the transportation needed for the celebration and Logan. Do you want me to keep the central Boston options in play if they require a transfer to reach Harvard Square?
Yes. Keep one good Cambridge option and the best central option near rapid transit. We can handle a transfer if the overall case is better.

I found three initial candidates. The Sheraton Commander is about a 6-minute walk from 10 Garden Street. Revere Hotel Boston Common is near Arlington station, with one transfer to the Red Line for Harvard. A lower-priced citizenM room downtown appears in the results, but its one-king room has a stated maximum occupancy of two and does not allow a rollaway, so it cannot accommodate all three of you.
Drop citizenM. What rooms at the other two are genuinely valid for three?

At the Sheraton Commander, the Traditional Room with two queen beds has a maximum occupancy of four, so three guests are permitted without an added bed. At Revere, the Premium Room with two queen beds and a balcony also has a maximum occupancy of four. I confirmed both room descriptions against the three-guest booking path; neither requires a rollaway or sofa bed.
Good. For family leisure stays like this, prioritize a balcony when one is available. It isn't mandatory, and I wouldn't throw out an otherwise good hotel just because it lacks one.

Understood. Revere gets an advantage on that point, while the Sheraton remains viable because it is much closer to the celebration. I’ll compare the exact totals and cancellation terms rather than eliminating it.
Give me the nightly breakdown with taxes. Also make sure neither quote quietly changes to two guests.

Both quotes are priced for two adults and one 12-year-old. Sheraton Commander, two-queen room: Friday $329, Saturday $349, Sunday $289, Monday $279, subtotal $1,246. Massachusetts and local lodging taxes add $184.91, for $1,430.91 total. Revere, premium two-queen room: Friday $299, Saturday $319, Sunday $249, Monday $239, subtotal $1,106. A $35 nightly destination fee adds $140, and taxes on the room and taxable fees add $184.96, for $1,430.96 total. The two lodging totals are effectively identical.
What does the Revere fee include? Don't count vague credits as savings.

The listed inclusions are standard Wi-Fi, fitness-center access, two bottled waters daily, and a daily food-and-beverage credit that expires each day. I have not subtracted any of those from the total or treated them as cash value. The payable four-night amount remains $1,430.96.
Now cancellation. I want the actual deadline in Boston time and what happens after it.

The Sheraton rate can be canceled without charge through 11:59 p.m. Eastern on Tuesday January 19. After that, the penalty is one night plus tax, approximately $377.71. The Revere rate can be canceled without charge through 6:00 p.m. Eastern on Wednesday January 20. After that, the stated penalty is the full stay amount of $1,430.96. Neither room requires prepayment under these rates.
Revere has the later deadline but a much worse penalty. Work out transportation for both. Include Friday from Logan, Saturday to the celebration, and the early Tuesday airport trip.

For the Sheraton: Friday rideshare from Logan is about 25-45 minutes and $34-$52. The celebration is a 6-minute walk, so Saturday transport is $0. For Tuesday’s 7:10 a.m. flight, leave the hotel around 5:10 a.m.; a rideshare should take 20-30 minutes and cost $31-$47. Expected required local transport is $65-$99, making lodging plus transport $1,495.91-$1,529.91. Public transit from Logan is possible Friday but takes roughly 55-70 minutes with transfers.
And Revere? Use transit where it is practical, but not for the predawn airport run.

From Logan on Friday, take the airport shuttle to the Blue Line, transfer to the Green Line, and walk from Arlington; allow 45-60 minutes. Three adult fares total about $7.20. On Saturday, Arlington to Park Street, then the Red Line to Harvard plus the walk takes 35-45 minutes each way; six rides total $14.40. Tuesday, leave at 5:20 a.m. for a 15-25 minute rideshare to Logan, estimated at $25-$38. Required transport totals $46.60-$59.60, bringing Revere to $1,477.56-$1,490.56.
So Revere is only about $5 to $52 cheaper all-in, depending on rideshare pricing. Check whether that Saturday estimate leaves enough margin for a 2:00 start.

Yes. Leaving Revere at 12:55 p.m. gives about 65 minutes for the Green-to-Red trip and final walk, including roughly 20 minutes of disruption margin. A more relaxed departure would be 12:40. From the Sheraton, leaving at 1:40 p.m. is sufficient for the short walk. After the event, Revere is approximately 35-45 minutes by transit or 20-35 minutes by rideshare; the Sheraton is walkable.
Any practical issue with Owen in either room? I want a real sleeping place, not language suggesting the third guest can just squeeze in.

No. Each retained room has two physical queen beds in the published room configuration, and the reservation path explicitly accepts two adults plus one child age 12. Owen would have one queen bed while you and Daniel use the other. There is no rollaway request, shared sofa bed, or occupancy exception involved.
Choose the stronger one, but don't reserve it. I care about the room and total, but be honest about the celebration commute and cancellation risk.

Choose Revere Hotel Boston Common, Premium Room with two queen beds, for four nights, but do not book yet. It legally and practically accommodates all three of you, provides two fixed sleeping surfaces, and totals $1,430.96 including taxes and mandatory fees. With transit Friday and Saturday plus a Tuesday rideshare, the expected combined cost is $1,477.56-$1,490.56. Leave at 12:40 p.m. Saturday for the 2:00 celebration and at 5:20 a.m. Tuesday for Logan. Its weaknesses are the 35-45 minute celebration trip and the full-stay penalty after 6:00 p.m. Eastern Wednesday January 20. Keep the Sheraton Commander two-queen room as the backup: $1,430.91 lodging, $1,495.91-$1,529.91 with rideshares, a 6-minute walk to the event, free cancellation through 11:59 p.m. Eastern Tuesday January 19, then an estimated $377.71 penalty. Flights remain selected, not booked: JetBlue ORD-BOS Friday 8:05-11:23 a.m. and BOS-ORD Tuesday 7:10-9:13 a.m., currently $936 total for three.
